name: Uno
subtitle: The classic colour clash.
rules: Match the colour, number or symbol.
Call UNO when one card remains.
Empty your hand first. Draw four may be challenged.

name: Uno No Mercy
subtitle: Friendships, on hard mode.
rules: Match the colour, number or symbol.
Call UNO when one card remains.
25 cards means elimination; stack equal or higher draws.

name: Monopoly Deal
subtitle: Build an empire, one card at a time.
rules: Collect three complete property sets in different colours.
Draw two and play up to three cards per turn. Keep at most seven.
Bank money to pay rent. Counter attacks with Just Say No.

name: Monopoly Deal No Mercy
subtitle: Games house deck. No mercy.
rules: Collect three complete property sets in different colours.
Draw two and play up to three cards per turn. Keep at most seven.
Debt must be settled before your own plays. Nothing is safe.
Games house deck: 18 money cards — 5×1M, 4×2M, 3×3M, 2×4M, 2×5M, 1×10M, 1×15M. Printed action effects; money copy counts are a house convention.

name: Texas Hold’em
subtitle: Find your seat at the table.
rules: Make the best five-card hand from your two cards and five community cards.
Blinds 1/2. Each player starts with 200 free chips.
No-limit betting, side pots and split pots are supported.

name: Rummy
subtitle: A good hand comes together.
rules: Draw one, discard one, and arrange your 13 cards.
Declare with two sequences, including one pure sequence.
Points format. Jokers are wild; maximum loss is 80 points.

name: Teen Patti
subtitle: Three cards. Endless possibilities.
rules: Play blind or look at your three cards and play seen.
Trail beats sequence, colour, pair and high card.
Free chips only. Boot 1; base stake cap 64; pot cap 1024.

name: Blackjack
subtitle: A little luck. A little nerve.
rules: Get closer to 21 than the dealer without going over.
Blackjack pays 3:2. Ties return your stake.
Split pairs or double on two cards.

name: Skyjo
subtitle: Small numbers. Big surprises.
rules: Reveal two cards, then trade to lower your grid's score.
Three matching revealed cards in a column disappear.
At 100 total points, the lowest score wins.

name: Pop Tarot
subtitle: Your plot twist is in the cards.
rules: Think of a question, or simply see what comes up.
Pick three cards: where you are, what is shifting, your next move.
Get an AI-written personal reading with a pop-culture twist.
A playful reflection, not a prediction or professional advice.

name: Four in a Row
subtitle: One more move. Four in a row.
rules: Drop a disc into an open column.
Connect four horizontally, vertically or diagonally to win.
A full board without a four-in-a-row is a draw.

name: Reversi
subtitle: Turn the whole table around.
rules: Place a disc to bracket and flip an opponent’s line.
You must pass when no capturing placement is available.
When neither player can move, the most discs wins.

name: Word Agents
subtitle: One clue. A room full of possibilities.
rules: Two spymasters know the key. Their teams see only the words.
Give a one-word clue and a number; your team gets up to one extra guess.
Find all your agents and avoid the assassin.

name: Gem Market
subtitle: Small gems. A brilliant empire.
rules: Collect gems, reserve a card or buy a development each turn.
Developments discount future purchases; patrons reward a balanced engine.
At 15 prestige, finish the round. Most prestige wins; fewer developments breaks a tie.

name: Checkers
subtitle: A small move. A clever little trap.
rules: Move diagonally forward on dark squares. Captures are compulsory.
Finish every available jump with the same piece; choose any capture path.
Reach the far row to become a king. Crowning ends that turn; kings move either way.
Win when the other player has no pieces or legal move. Threefold repetition or 40 moves each without a capture/man move draws.

name: Mancala
subtitle: Sow a little. Steal a march.
rules: Kalah: four seeds in each of twelve pits, with two stores starting empty.
Choose a pit on your side. Sow counterclockwise, including your store and skipping your opponent’s.
Finish in your store to play again. Finish in your empty pit opposite seeds to capture both.
When either side empties, sweep the other side into its own store. Most seeds wins; equal stores draw.

name: Flip 7
subtitle: One more card. Famous last words.
rules: 94-card deck. Hit for a card or Stay to bank your round points. Duplicate numbers bust.
Freeze banks a target; Flip Three forces up to three cards; Second Chance saves one duplicate.
During Flip Three, resolve extra Freeze/Flip Three cards after the batch unless the drawer busts.
Seven distinct numbers end the round and add 15. Double numbers before adding modifiers.
Highest score at 200 wins after the round. Tied leaders play on. Resolved actions stay out until round end.

name: Trio
subtitle: A little memory. A perfect three.
rules: Simple individual mode. Three copies each of numbers 1–12; sorted private hands.
Reveal a table card or any hand’s current lowest or highest card, including your own.
A mismatch ends your turn. Three equal numbers earn a trio.
Collect three trios, or the trio of sevens, to win. Review reveals before continuing.

name: Azul
subtitle: Your next masterpiece, one tile at a time.
rules: Standard colored wall. Draft every tile of one color from one factory or the center.
Put the draft in one compatible pattern line. Excess goes to your floor.
Completed lines place one wall tile and score linked neighbors; unfinished lines stay.
Floor costs are 1,1,2,2,2,3,3. The first center taker gets the marker and starts next round.
A complete wall row ends the round and match. Bonuses: row 2, column 7, color 10. Ties favor more complete rows.
Games exhaustion convention: if no tiles can form a new offer, finish with normal bonuses. Unfinished lines stay put.

name: Spill or Chill
subtitle: A good story. Zero pressure.
rules: Games original house rules: 48 original prompts, two spotlight turns per person.
The spotlight player answers aloud and chooses Share, Chill or Pass.
Share and Chill both earn one participation point. Pass earns zero.
No answers are recorded. The most participation points wins.
The spotlight player advances each reveal. Equal highest scores share the win.
Sip prompts are optional, use any drink and never affect scoring. Passing is always available.

name: Most Likely
subtitle: Secret votes. Extremely public personalities.
rules: Games original house rules: 48 original prompts, two spotlight turns per person.
Everyone secretly votes for another player, or passes. No self-votes.
Votes lock on submission and reveal together. Tied positive leaders each earn a point.
All-pass rounds award no points. Most spotlight points wins.
The spotlight player advances each reveal. Equal highest scores share the win.
Sip prompts are optional, use any drink and never affect scoring. Passing is always available.

name: Hot Seat
subtitle: How well do your friends really know you?
rules: Games original house rules: 48 original prompts, two spotlight turns per person.
The spotlight player privately chooses A or B; everyone else predicts their choice.
Everyone may pass. Decisions lock and reveal only after everyone submits.
Correct predictions earn one point; a spotlight pass awards none. Most points wins.
The spotlight player advances each reveal. Equal highest scores share the win.
Sip prompts are optional, use any drink and never affect scoring. Passing is always available.

name: The Gang
subtitle: One crew. Three vaults. No poker faces spared.
rules: Basic cooperative game. Win three vaults before three alarms. No betting or money.
Two private pocket cards; reveal the flop, turn and river across four chip rounds.
Take or steal a current-color chip, or return yours. One star means weakest; the highest means strongest.
The instant everyone holds a chip, that round ends. Earlier chip colors remain as public history.
Reveal in red-chip order. Best five-of-seven poker hands must be equally strong or stronger each time; exact ties are fine.
Do not share information about your own hand. Challenge/specialist and advanced modes are not included.

name: 6 nimmt!
subtitle: Pick a number. Dodge the sixth card.
rules: Classic 104-card deck. Ten private cards each; four public rows. Lowest penalty total wins.
Everyone locks one secret card, then all reveal together. Numbers resolve from lowest to highest.
Each card follows the greatest row-end number below it. The sixth card takes that row's five cards as penalties.
A card below every row end must take a row of its owner's choice, becoming its new starter.
Penalty values: ordinary 1; ending in five 2; multiples of ten 3; multiples of eleven 5; 55 has 7.
After all ten cards, total penalties. At 66 or more, finish the round: lowest total wins and equal lowest totals tie.

name: Sea Salt & Paper
subtitle: A tiny ocean. A tide of possibilities.
rules: 58-card base edition. Take a discard top, or draw two, keep one and discard the other.
Play duos: crabs search one discard, boats repeat your turn, fish draw, shark+swimmer steal.
Played and unplayed cards both score. At 7+ points, choose Stop or bet on Last Chance.
Last Chance reveals/protects hands. A successful caller scores cards+color; others color only. Failed caller scores color only.
Stock exhaustion at turn end scores nothing. Targets 40/35/30 at 2/3/4 seats; all four mermaids win instantly.

name: boop.
subtitle: Tiny kittens. Delightfully big moves.
rules: Place a kitten or available cat in any empty square on the 6×6 bed.
Adjacent pieces boop one space away. Occupied destinations block; no chain reactions.
Kittens cannot push cats. Off-bed pieces return to their owner's pool.
After booping, graduate one line of three into cats; with eight pieces down, you may return one instead.
Only the active player checks: three adult cats in a line or eight adult cats on the bed wins.
